question.problem: Consider the function $f(x)=2x+\sqrt{x}.$ Given that $y=f(x)$ is invertible throughout its domain, determine $({f}^{-1})^{′}(1).$
question.worked_solution:
To determine $({f}^{-1})^{′}(1),$ we use the following formula:

$$
{({f}^{-1})}^{′}(1)=\frac{1}{{f}^{′}({f}^{-1}(1))}
$$

First, we calculate the value of ${f}^{-1}(1).$ To do this, we solve the equation ${f}^{-1}(1)=x.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{-1}(1) & =x \\ f(x) & =1 \\ 2x+\sqrt{x} & =1 \\ \sqrt{x} & =1-2x \\ x & =1-4x+4{x}^{2} \\ 4{x}^{2}-5x+1 & =0 \\ (4x-1)(x-1) & =0 \\ x & =\frac{1}{4},\,1.\end{aligned}
$$

Checking the solutions, we notice that only $x=\frac{1}{4}$ satisfies the equation $2x+\sqrt{x}=1.$ Therefore, we discard $x=1$ and conclude that ${f}^{-1}(1)=\frac{1}{4}.$

Now, we calculate ${f}^{′}(\frac{1}{4}),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =2x+\sqrt{x} \\ {f}^{′}(x) & =2+\frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}} \\ {f}^{′}(\frac{1}{4}) & =2+\frac{1}{2\sqrt{(\frac{1}{4})}} \\ {f}^{′}(\frac{1}{4}) & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{({f}^{-1})}^{′}(1) & =\frac{1}{{f}^{′}({f}^{-1}(1))} \\  & =\frac{1}{{f}^{′}(\frac{1}{4})} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
